tasks.old_behavior: After r1918022, when a process_connection hook returned OK with cs->pub.state still CONN_STATE_PROCESSING, the MPM performed POLLIN/POLLOUT on the underlying socket (based on sense), waiting for I/O readiness using Timeout before calling back the process_connection hooks again. This changed the earlier semantics where OK+CONN_STATE_PROCESSING was equivalent to lingering close.
tasks.new_behavior: This patch restores the earlier semantics: when a process_connection hook returns OK and cs->pub.state remains CONN_STATE_PROCESSING, the MPM degrades to lingering close processing. If a hook wants the MPM to wait for I/O and call back, it must return the newly introduced AGAIN(-4) return code while maintaining CONN_STATE_PROCESSING state. Additionally, DONE return value is now mapped to OK (no longer treated as an independent code).
tasks.compatibility_reason: This change has significant compatibility impact on third-party modules using Event MPM: (1) Any module relying on r1918022's 'OK+CONN_STATE_PROCESSING -> POLLIN/POLLOUT' behavior will break, connections will be unexpectedly closed; (2) Modules wanting the I/O wait mechanism must be modified to return AGAIN instead of OK, but can check ap_mpm_query(AP_MPMQ_CAN_AGAIN) first for graceful fallback; (3) The DONE->OK mapping may affect code paths checking for DONE return. This is the root cause compatibility change of this patch.
tasks.test_recommendation: Build httpd with GCOV instrumentation. Write a test module implementing process_connection hook: verify that OK+CONN_STATE_PROCESSING triggers lingering close (not POLLIN/POLLOUT); verify that AGAIN+CONN_STATE_PROCESSING puts the connection back in the pollset for I/O events. Also verify DONE->OK mapping does not break third-party modules.

tasks.old_behavior: h2_c1_run() returned apr_status_t type, logged errors and closed connection only when APR_STATUS_IS_EOF(status). In non-keepalive case, set cs->state=CONN_STATE_PROCESSING or CONN_STATE_WRITE_COMPLETION (controlled by H2_USE_STATE_PROCESSING compile-time macro). h2_c1_hook_process_connection always returned OK.
tasks.new_behavior: h2_c1_run() returns int type, uses status!=APR_SUCCESS for error checking (covers EOF and all other non-success states). New mpm_can_again static variable (queried via ap_mpm_query(AP_MPMQ_CAN_AGAIN)): when MPM supports it and non-keepalive, returns AGAIN(-4) with cs->state=CONN_STATE_PROCESSING; otherwise uses CONN_STATE_WRITE_COMPLETION+clogging_input_filters=1 as compat fallback. h2_c1_hook_process_connection propagates h2_c1_run()'s return value to MPM instead of always returning OK.
tasks.compatibility_reason: (1) Return type changed from apr_status_t to int: while AGAIN=-4 is unknown to old MPMs, old MPMs cannot set AP_MPMQ_CAN_AGAIN so the module won't return AGAIN; (2) Error handling relaxed from APR_STATUS_IS_EOF to status!=APR_SUCCESS, which may cause connection close on non-fatal error states (e.g., APR_EAGAIN); (3) clogging_input_filters side effect changes MPM's subsequent connection processing path; (4) h2_c1.h still declares apr_status_t while implementation uses int, causing potential compile warnings.
tasks.test_recommendation: Build Apache httpd with mod_http2: verify fallback to clogging_input_filters path on MPMs without AP_MPMQ_CAN_AGAIN; verify AGAIN return triggers correct poll callback on capable MPMs; confirm connection close behavior on non-EOF error states meets expectations; run mod_http2 existing test suite for regressions.
